task_instance: Given a GitHub issue URL (e.g. https://github.com/getsentry/sentry-python/issues/1234) and the open PR for the current branch, resolve the issue's Linear ticket from its linear-linkback comment and append a '#### Issues' block (Resolves: #1234, Resolves: PY-2357) to the PR description via `gh pr edit`.
blocker_detail: The skill's core deliverable is mutating a real PR on GitHub (`gh pr edit --body ...`) after reading a real issue's comments (`gh issue view --json comments`) via the GitHub API. This is a write to an external service, which the task's safety rules explicitly forbid ('No git push; no pull requests, issues, comments or any other writes to external services') and also forbid working around by using the disallowed GitHub MCP tools. Separately, `gh auth status` shows the only available token (GH_TOKEN) is invalid, so even a read-only rehearsal (`gh issue view`, `gh pr view`) against a real repo/PR would need credentials I'm instructed not to seek out. Since there is no real PR/issue in this repo to safely target and no permitted path to writing a PR description on GitHub, the actual deliverable (an updated PR description on GitHub containing the Issues block) cannot be produced or verified in this sandbox. I did not attempt a workaround (e.g. faking a local 'gh' shim) because that would not exercise or verify the real deliverable the skill promises (an actual updated GitHub PR), it would only test the text-formatting/regex logic in isolation.
evidence: Ran `which gh` -> /usr/local/bin/gh (gh CLI is present). Ran `gh auth status` -> 'Failed to log in to github.com using token (GH_TOKEN)' / 'The token in GH_TOKEN is invalid.' Confirmed via SKILL.md (steps 1,3,4,6) that the workflow requires `gh pr view`, `gh issue view --repo ... --json comments`, and `gh pr edit --body ...` against a real GitHub repo/PR/issue — i.e., live external-service reads and a write. Per the safety rules (no writes to external services, no searching for/using credentials, no GitHub MCP tool use), this could not be attempted against a real target, so the deliverable (an actual PR description updated with a '#### Issues' block referencing the GitHub issue and its Linear key) was not produced.
